sentences.text: Bashanosaurus primitivus is an extinct stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic period in what is now Asia.
This genus contains only one species, Bashanosaurus primitivus, which was formally named in a 2022 article.
The animal was a quadrupedal herbivore characterized by a row of plates and spines running from its neck to its tail, along with four incomplete osteoderms consisting of one spine and three plates.
Researchers note that the specific morphology of these dermal plates is considered a unique trait of the species.
Fossils of this dinosaur show a unique mix of features typically found in both adult and immature animals.
Seven dorsal vertebrae are known from the genus, and the centra of these vertebrae are flat on both ends.
Anatomical studies reveal that Bashanosaurus had a poorly developed acromial process on its scapula.
Additionally, the fourth trochanter of the femur is uniquely positioned below the middle of the shaft.
Based on comparisons with Huayangosaurus, researchers estimate the animal may have been about 3 meters long, though the holotype measured 2.8 meters in length.
Bashanosaurus is the oldest named stegosaur known from Asia and is currently the oldest known stegosaur, replacing Adratiklit as the oldest known species.
The tail armor of this dinosaur likely served as a defensive structure against predators.
Fossils were found in a quarry discovered in 2016 in Chongqing, China, specifically within the Shaximiao Formation in Yunyang.
The fossils were recovered from the "Dinosaur Fossil Wall" locality of the Lower Member of the Shaximiao Formation in Yunyang County.
The known material consists of two partial skeletons and a vertebra from a third individual.
The holotype includes limb bones, back and tail vertebrae, plates, and a spike.
As one of the most basal stegosaurs, the tail armor likely served as a defensive structure against predators.
The bonebed containing Bashanosaurus fossils also yielded sauropods such as Omeisaurus puxiani, Shunosaurus, and Yuzhoulong.
The non-dinosaurian fauna at the site included pterosaurs, turtles, crocodyliforms, pliosaurid plesiosaurs, therapsids, fish, and amphibians.

Dai and colleagues (2022) classified Bashanosaurus as the most basal member of the Stegosauria, placing it as the sister taxon to Chungkingosaurus, and named both the genus and species in that same year.
However, a 2025 study by Sánchez-Fenollosa and Cobos placed Bashanosaurus within the Huayangosauridae clade as the sister taxon to Huayangosaurus.
Bashanosaurus lived during the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 169 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Bashanosaurus is estimated from 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.

It is debated whether the known Bashanosaurus specimens were fully grown, suggesting the animal may have been capable of growing larger, and it is also debated whether later phylogenetic analyses confirm the exact placement of Bashanosaurus, though results have been very similar to the original description.
